question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation in nursing care?

options.A: To completely cure chronic underlying pathologies
options.B: To eliminate the need for any follow-up care
options.C: To maximize a person's independence and functional level
options.D: To keep patients admitted in hospital wards long-term

explanation: You've got this! Rehab is all about helping your patients live life to the fullest and do as much for themselves as possible, even if a chronic condition is still there. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h1)

question: Why do patients need a broad support network during rehabilitation?

options.A: Families prefer to shift all medical duties to non-governmental groups
options.B: Hospitals lack the space to house recovering patients for more than a week
options.C: Doctors cannot manage chronic conditions without government supervision
options.D: Recovery continues long after hospital discharge and requires help from many sources

explanation: Healing doesn't stop just because the patient goes home. Family, community, and healthcare teams all team up to keep the momentum going! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h1)

question: What is the most important ingredient for success in personal rehabilitation?

options.D: Strict supervision by a medical doctor

explanation: A patient's own drive and willingness to try make the biggest difference in their recovery journey. You are their guide, but they do the heavy lifting! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h2)

question: A patient refuses their home exercises and seems down. How should you view this as a nurse?

options.A: They clearly want their condition to deteriorate permanently
options.B: They are purposely wasting the healthcare team's valuable time
options.C: They have no right to question their prescribed care plan
options.D: They are likely overwhelmed and need support rather than judgment

explanation: When patients pull back, it's often burnout or emotional distress speaking. A little empathy goes a long way in helping them trust the process again. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h2)

question: What is a major risk for family members who care for a loved one long-term without a break?
explanation: Looking after someone takes a massive physical and emotional toll. Always remember to check on the caregivers too—they need support to stay strong! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h3)

question: You are getting a stroke survivor ready to go home. What is the best way to involve the family?

options.A: Teach them safe transfer techniques and assess their coping abilities
options.B: Assume they already know how to handle home therapy without guidance
options.C: Tell them to hire paid nurses so they do not have to do any work
options.D: Instruct them to isolate the patient to prevent any accidental injuries

explanation: Giving families practical skills and making sure they feel ready keeps everyone safe and lowers stress at home. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h3)

question: What is the main goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR)?

options.A: To isolate individuals with disabilities in specialized camps
options.B: To force families to relocate to urban rehabilitation centers
options.C: To make support services accessible at the grassroots level
options.D: To replace all tertiary hospitals with small village clinics

explanation: CBR brings care right to where people live, making sure help is close to home instead of locked away in distant city hospitals. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h4)

question: How does community-based rehabilitation help fight against social stigma?

options.A: By involving local leaders and educating the public about disabilities
options.B: By forcing communities to build expensive private hospitals
options.C: By restricting public gatherings for people with chronic illnesses
options.D: By hiding individuals with disabilities away from public view

explanation: Education clears up misunderstandings. When local communities learn together, they start seeing the person first, not the disability. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h4)

question: Which body carries the primary duty of passing national disability rights laws?
explanation: The government sets the legal foundation and framework needed to protect and support citizens living with disabilities across the country. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h5)

question: Why is government funding for assistive devices like wheelchairs so important?

options.A: It makes devices like wheelchairs and hearing aids affordable for low-income citizens
options.B: It ensures that doctors receive higher salaries than other public workers
options.C: It prevents private hospitals from offering any medical services
options.D: It eliminates the need for physical therapy exercises at home

explanation: Good assistive tools can be very expensive. Government support helps bridge the financial gap so vulnerable patients aren't left behind. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h5)

question: What is a major way non-governmental organizations (NGOs) help in healthcare?

options.A: Controlling the licensure of medical doctors and nurses
options.B: Collecting taxes from local citizens to fund state budgets
options.C: Replacing all national laws with private organizational rules
options.D: Filling service gaps left by underfunded public systems

explanation: When public resources fall short, NGOs often step in with extra supplies, outreach, and hands-on help for communities in need. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h6)

question: How do advocacy groups empower individuals who are going through rehabilitation?

options.A: By taking away their legal right to make personal decisions
options.B: By forcing them to rely exclusively on charitable handouts
options.C: By isolating them from mainstream political conversations
options.D: By giving them a collective voice to lobby for their rights

explanation: There is strength in numbers! Advocacy groups help people join together to demand better accessibility, fair treatment, and policy changes. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h6)

question: What does inter-sectoral collaboration mean in the context of rehabilitation?

options.A: Working together across different fields like education, housing, and health
options.B: Requiring every patient to work in government offices
options.C: Merging all non-governmental groups into a single department
options.D: Leaving all recovery decisions strictly to hospital physicians

explanation: A patient's life involves more than just medicine. Bringing education, housing, and health sectors together ensures all of their needs are met. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h7)

question: Why is making workplaces accessible just as important as medical treatment?

options.A: Financial independence and social integration depend on the ability to work
options.B: Employers are legally required to provide physical therapy on-site
options.C: Medical insurance is only valid for employed citizens
options.D: Workers cannot leave their homes unless they have a job

explanation: Medical healing is only the first step. Having an accessible job allows people to support themselves and truly feel part of society again. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h7)
